source.title: SGD with large step sizes learns sparse features
source.authors: Maksym Andriushchenko; A. Varre; Loucas Pillaud-Vivien; Nicolas Flammarion

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendix; no document or truncation problem noted.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests how SGD step-size schedules affect generalization and feature sparsity, but does not test the specific conditions or measurements named in V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own comparisons of step-size schedules and their effects on test performance and feature sparsity. Its theoretical discussion and cited findings are not recorded as empirical rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests learning-rate schedules and sparse feature learning, rather than any V1–V8 comparison. Its discussion of small batches and flatness supplies neither a fixed-budget batch-size comparison nor magnitude-aware sharpness measurements.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors report that large-step-size loss stabilization enables hidden stochastic dynamics associated with sparse feature learning and better generalization for longer schedules. They propose an SDE explanation, with theoretical justification in simple models and empirical evidence in larger networks. Causality between feature sparsity and test error on natural datasets remains unresolved. The main sparsity experiments omit explicit regularization, but Figure 1 uses weight decay.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies SGD step-size schedules and measures test performance and feature sparsity; it does not apply the interventions or measurements specified by V1–V8.
record.method_sensitivity: Test performance and feature sparsity vary with step size and the length of the large-step-size phase; warmup is used in some settings to achieve loss stabilization.

fits_no_version.finding: Large-step-size SGD schedules with longer loss stabilization improve held-out performance and produce sparser features in the tested regression and image-classification settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning-rate schedules can alter SGD's implicit regularization: longer loss stabilization can improve generalization while reducing the fraction of distinct active features.

fits_no_version.finding: Full-batch GD exhibits loss stabilization without the test-loss improvement or comparable sparsification obtained with SGD in the diagonal linear-network experiment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss stabilization alone is insufficient for the generalization and sparsification benefits observed with stochastic updates in this setting.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning; Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 202, 2023
record.problems: The natural-data feature-sparsity and test-error association is correlational; the authors say its causal relation remains unresolved. Several reported comparisons are presented in figures without exact values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Other schedule, dataset, architecture, and layer results are shown in Figures 2, 4–7, and 14–17, but their individual values are figure-only and the text does not state separate numerical outcomes for each condition. Figure 9’s SDE validation is not included because it evaluates the authors’ model of the SGD dynamics rather than the claim’s generalization finding.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed for interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets, including recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on dataset size, strength, or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps and rankings against norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The original tests/T2 classification is inconsistent with the absence of any tested claim version. Learning-rate effects cannot substitute for batch-size effects, and feature sparsity cannot substitute for magnitude-aware sharpness. States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8; this does not dispute the paper's reported schedule effects.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or random-label test accuracy comparison.
No network-width sweep around the interpolation threshold.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected architectures.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD.
No batch-size comparison under a fixed epoch budget.
The study measures feature sparsity and Jacobian rank, not magnitude-aware sharpness or the tested norm- and margin-based measures.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Compared small-step-size training with large-step-size schedules decayed at different points.

conditions.value: η = 1.5, decay at 10%, 30%, or 50% of epochs; compared with η = 0.007

rows.value: 12% vs. 35% test error, depending on step size and schedule
rows.note: The caption states the reported range; the supplied text does not assign each value to a specific schedule.
rows.check: The reported 12% versus 35% test-error comparison is supported, but measures a learning-rate schedule effect outside V1–V8. These are endpoints across schedules, not separately identified condition values.

rows.subject: DenseNet-100-12
rows.operation_detail: Compared a small step size with large-step-size schedules and warmup, decayed at different epochs.

conditions.value: small step size η = 0.07 versus η = 0.75 with warmup

rows.note: The text reports this comparison as an example of suboptimal generalization with small step sizes.
rows.check: The 60% versus 35% test-error comparison is supported, but no claim version concerns this learning-rate intervention.

rows.subject: DenseNet-100-12
rows.operation_detail: Compared feature sparsity during small-step-size training and large-step-size schedules.

conditions.value: small step size versus large step size with warmup

rows.value: typically 50%-60% for small step sizes vs. 10%-20% for larger step sizes at block 4
rows.note: The paper says feature sparsity and test error decrease together, but says whether they are causally related on natural datasets remains to be seen.
rows.check: Feature sparsity is not magnitude-aware sharpness or another V1–V8 outcome. The 50%–60% versus 10%–20% ranges summarize typical block-4 results across the deep-network experiments; the text does not identify them specifically as CIFAR-100 basic-setting values. Lower coefficients mean sparser features.

rows.subject: Diagonal linear networks
rows.operation_detail: Compared full-batch gradient descent loss-stabilization schedules with SGD.
rows.note: The caption states that full-batch GD loss stabilization did not improve test loss; no numerical test-loss values are recoverable from the text.
rows.check: Figure 11 explicitly reports no test-loss improvement from full-batch GD loss stabilization, but this is outside V1–V8. Its dataset is synthetic sparse linear regression, using the Section 3.1 setup, rather than unspecified. The absence statement applies to improvement from GD stabilization, not to a claim version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
